<objective>
Build the **session_id → tmux pane map** (PILOT-03) — the no-mis-routing keystone. A SessionStart
hook (which already receives `session_id` + `cwd` on stdin and inherits `$TMUX_PANE`) writes a
per-session registry record; a SessionEnd hook removes it; the daemon-side `registry.py` joins a
live session to its pane and reconciles liveness so a missed SessionEnd (crash / kill -9) can never
mis-route.

This plan owns the `~/.claude/` bridge-layer hooks (D-08/D-09: in-bounds, reversible, additive — NOT
a violation of "external daemon") + their settings.json registration, plus the pure daemon-side
registry logic. It is parallel with plan 01 (disjoint files).

Purpose: PILOT-03 — every action targets the correct pane even with multiple concurrent sessions.
Output: 2 new hooks + settings.json registration; `autopilot/registry.py` GREEN.

NO action, NO keystroke, NO tmux install (that is plan 04). The hooks are pure metadata writers;
the daemon-side resolver is fixture-tested with a fake registry + stubbed `tmux`.
</objective>

<interfaces>
<!-- The SessionStart/SessionEnd hook contract (VERIFIED, RESEARCH §2.2) + the registry record shape. -->

SessionStart/SessionEnd hook stdin (CC docs mirror hooks.md):
- Common input fields include `session_id` and `cwd` (stdin JSON). The hook gets both directly.
- A hook process **inherits the parent environment** → the SessionStart hook inherits `$TMUX_PANE`
  from the CC process (which, per D-04, runs inside the tmux pane). THIS is the clean join.
  ⚠️ D-11: $TMUX_PANE inheritance is VERIFY-GATED (tmux not installed yet) — plan 04 proves it live.
  The hook MUST therefore degrade gracefully when `$TMUX_PANE` is absent (write `pane: null`, never crash).
- SessionStart `source` ∈ startup | resume | clear | compact. "SessionStart hooks run again on resume."
  ⇒ the registry write is an idempotent UPSERT keyed on session_id (resume may land in a DIFFERENT pane).
- SessionEnd reasons ∈ clear | resume | logout | prompt_input_exit | bypass_permissions_disabled | other;
  no decision control (side-effect only — fine for cleanup). A crash / kill -9 may emit NO SessionEnd
  ⇒ the daemon must NOT trust the registry for liveness (→ reconcile, D-10).
- SessionStart supports type:"command" only here; "runs on every session, so keep it fast" → a tiny hook.
- The 10s pipe-hang guard + exit-0-on-every-path discipline (mirror cco-compact-nudge.js).

Registry record (per-session file — chosen over one shared file to avoid write races, RESEARCH §5.3):
`~/.claude/.autopilot/registry.d/{session_id}.json`:
```json
{"session_id":"062b51ef-…","pane":"%5","cwd":"/Users/…/proj","pid":12345,"ts":1782076190,"source":"startup"}
```

tmux pane existence check (RESEARCH §2.3): `tmux list-panes -aF '#{pane_id}'` → the set of live `%N` ids.
Pane addressing is ALWAYS by `pane_id` (`%N`) — the unambiguous form; NEVER by session name (names collide).

Existing hook pattern to mirror (~/.claude/hooks/cco-compact-nudge.js lines 12-30):
- `setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 10000)` pipe-hang guard;
- reject `session_id` matching `/[/\\]|\.\./` before any path use;
- `process.exit(0)` on every path (a hook must never block the session).
</interfaces>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| SessionStart stdin → registry file | The hook interpolates `session_id` into a filename; `cwd`/`source` are written as metadata. Untrusted-ish (CC-supplied, but the id is filename-bound). |
| concurrent hooks → one registry dir | Multiple sessions' SessionStart hooks write the registry simultaneously. |
| registry record → daemon pane targeting | The `pane` value decides which terminal a future keystroke (Phase 20) hits — mis-routing = acting on the wrong session. |
| tmux subprocess → daemon | `tmux list-panes` output is parsed for liveness. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-19-04 | Tampering | `session_id`→filename in both hooks | mitigate | Reject `session_id` matching `/[/\\]|\.\./` before any path use (mirrors the existing hook). A crafted id can't escape `registry.d/`. |
| T-19-05 | Tampering / DoS | concurrent SessionStart registry writes | mitigate | Per-session file + atomic temp-write-then-rename (RESEARCH §5.3) — no two sessions share a file, so no interleaved-write corruption. |
| T-19-06 | Spoofing / mis-routing | `resolve_pane` keyed on the registry | mitigate | Addressing is by `pane_id` (`%N`) keyed on `session_id`, NEVER on the (collision-prone) session name (D-07/D-08). Tested: two records resolve without swap. |
| T-19-07 | Repudiation (stale liveness) | a missed SessionEnd (crash / kill -9) leaves a dangling record | mitigate | `reconcile` (D-10) drops any record whose pane is absent from `tmux list-panes` OR whose session has no fresh bridge — a dead session's pane is never targeted even if SessionEnd never fired. Tested both ways. |
| T-19-08 | Info disclosure | hook writes session metadata | accept | Metadata-only (session_id/pane/cwd/pid/ts/source) — NO transcript content (matches cco-log hygiene); the registry is under the user's own `~/.claude/`. Low value, local-only. |
</threat_model>
